component.name: org.nuxeo.agentic.ui.config
component.documentation:
The UI configuration of Nuxeo Agentic UI, contributed by Marketplace packages.
A customer ships their own package: package.xml declares a dependency on nuxeo-agentic-ui, which orders installation, and its component requires org.nuxeo.agentic.ui.config.defaults, which orders the contributions. The servlet serves the result, in contribution order, at /nuxeo/agentic-ui-config/ (bootstrap.json, manifest.json, layouts.json, layouts/, assets/), without authentication — nothing sensitive may be contributed. The browser merges the fragments in order, so a later package wins key by key.
Business apps are contributed here too, as app elements, and served by the app registry at /nuxeo/agentic-ui-apps/ after sign-in: apps.json lists the apps whose app.json names a group the person is in, and apps/{id}/{path} serves each one's files. Seeing an app is not a security control: Nuxeo's permissions still decide which records anyone reads.
With nuxeo.agentic.ui.layer.enabled=true, each app has a deployment layer too: an administrator's own versions of its layouts and queues, made in the layout designer, kept in the repository under /agentic-ui-layers, checked on every write with the app definition's validator, and live only once a second administrator approves them (nuxeo.agentic.ui.layer.selfApproval=true lets the same one). The registry serves a live file in place of the package's to the app's groups; the configuration servlet never reads the layer. Its addresses, for administrators alone, are apps/{id}/layer/{path}, apps/{id}/layer.json and layer.json, under /nuxeo/agentic-ui-apps/.

extension-point.name: configuration
extension-point.documentation:
JSON fragments, per-type layout files and image assets.
{ "labels": { "app.navbar.browse": "Contracts" } }
src is read from the contributing bundle; the json child is the inline form. A later fragment with the same name and layer replaces an earlier one in place, a later layout with the same type and mode replaces it whole, and enabled="false" removes either. A replacement that cannot be read, is too large or does not parse is rejected and the earlier one stays.
An app's src is its app.json, whose id must be the app's and whose groups say who sees it. Each file is a path below the directory that holds app.json, at one of an app definition's places: home.json, navigation.json, actions.json, queues/{id}.json, labels/{language}.json and tasks/{workflow}.{step}.layout.json. A later app with the same id replaces it whole, and enabled="false" removes it. An app.json that cannot be used refuses the app; any other file that cannot be read, is over 1 MiB or does not parse is left out on its own.
